title: Quantitative Methods in Finance
abstract: arXiv:2601.12896v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: These lecture notes provide a comprehensive introduction to Quantitative Methods in Finance (QMF), designed for graduate students in finance and economics with heterogeneous programming backgrounds. The material develops a unified toolkit combining probability theory, statistics, numerical methods, and empirical modeling, with a strong emphasis on implementation in Python. Core topics include random variables and distributions, moments and dependence, simulation and Monte Carlo methods, numerical optimization, root-finding, and time-series models commonly used in finance and macro-finance. Particular attention is paid to translating theoretical concepts into reproducible code, emphasizing vectorization, numerical stability, and interpretation of outputs. The notes progressively bridge theory and practice through worked examples and exercises covering asset pricing intuition, risk measurement, forecasting, and empirical analysis. By f

translated_abstract: 这些讲义对金融学中的定量方法（QMF）进行了全面介绍，专为具有不同编程背景的金融与经济学研究生设计。该材料构建了一个统一的工具包，融合了概率论、统计学、数值方法和实证建模，并特别强调使用Python进行实现。核心主题包括随机变量与分布、矩与相依性、模拟与蒙特卡洛方法、数值优化、求根方法，以及金融和宏观金融领域常用的时间序列模型。讲义尤其注重将理论概念转化为可复现的代码，强调向量化、数值稳定性以及输出结果的解释。通过涵盖资产定价直觉、风险度量、预测和实证分析的实例与练习，这些讲义逐步架起了理论与实践之间的桥梁。
tldr: 这是一套面向金融与经济学研究生的定量方法讲义，构建了融合概率统计、数值方法与Python实现的统一工具包，通过可复现代码与实例练习架起金融理论与实证实践之间的桥梁。
en_tdlr: These lecture notes provide graduate students with a unified Python-based toolkit combining probability, statistics, and numerical methods for finance, bridging theory and practice through reproducible code, worked examples, and exercises.
